questions.text: In a PHP website, where does PHP code normally run?
questions.explanation:
PHP is a server-side language. The server executes it and sends the output to the browser.

Student note: Know the difference between PHP (server-side) and JavaScript (often browser-side).

questions.text: Which of these is commonly used to serve and run PHP pages on a local development computer?
questions.explanation:
Apache serves HTTP requests and hands PHP pages to the PHP interpreter.

Student note: XAMPP bundles tools such as Apache, PHP and MySQL for local testing.

questions.text: A file has a .php extension. Which statement about HTML in it is correct?
options: It may contain both HTML and PHP
questions.correctAnswer: It may contain both HTML and PHP
questions.explanation:
PHP scripts may include ordinary HTML outside PHP blocks.

Student note: You can switch between HTML and PHP using opening and closing PHP tags.

questions.text: Which sequence makes the most sense after finishing a PHP/MySQL application locally?
options: Set up hosting and database, upload files, import data and test configuration
Upload only screenshots of the application
Rename all PHP files to TXT and send them by email
Delete the local database before publishing
questions.correctAnswer: Set up hosting and database, upload files, import data and test configuration
questions.explanation:
Publishing needs both application files and a database/configuration that works on the remote server.

Student note: On a real host verify credentials, HTTPS, file permissions and that private secrets are not publicly exposed.

questions.text: Create a PHP function called wishSuccess() that takes one module code and displays a good-luck message containing that code.
aiRubric: Defines a function with a parameter
Displays the supplied module code in a good-luck message
questions.explanation:
A function groups reusable steps; its parameter supplies a different module code each time.

Student note: Parameters are names in a function definition; arguments are the values passed when calling it.

questions.text: Make a PHP array containing ICT2613, ICT2612 and ICT1513. Use a for loop to call wishSuccess() once for each code.
aiRubric: Defines array of three module codes
Does not skip or access outside the array
questions.explanation:
A for loop uses the index to process one array element at a time.

Student note: Use $i < count($codes), not <=, because PHP numeric array positions start at zero.

questions.text: What is the main reason to use htmlspecialchars() when displaying visitor-entered text on a webpage?
options: It converts HTML-sensitive characters to entities
questions.correctAnswer: It converts HTML-sensitive characters to entities
questions.explanation:
Converting characters such as < and > helps avoid interpreting user text as HTML.

Student note: For safe HTML output, prefer htmlspecialchars($value, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8').

questions.text: Three HTML radio inputs share the same name but have different values. What does this arrangement allow?
options: Only one option in that group can be chosen
The browser submits none of them
The form automatically creates a database
questions.correctAnswer: Only one option in that group can be chosen
questions.explanation:
Radio buttons with the same name form a single-choice group.

Student note: Checkboxes are different: several can be selected independently.

questions.text: Write a simple HTML form that sends a chosen module code by POST to question3.php, using two radio buttons and a submit button.
questions.correctAnswer:
<form action="question3.php" method="post">
 <label><input type="radio" name="module_code" value="ICT2613">ICT2613</label>
 <label><input type="radio" name="module_code" value="ICT2612">ICT2612</label>
 <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
questions.explanation:
The form action picks a receiving PHP script; POST sends values in the request body.

Student note: POST avoids placing form values in the URL, but HTTPS and input validation are still needed.

questions.text: Build an associative array that maps ICT2613 to PHP, ICT2612 to Java, and ICT1513 to JavaScript. Show the language for a submitted module_code, when the code exists.
aiRubric: Indexes associative array by module code
questions.explanation:
Associative arrays use meaningful keys rather than numeric positions.

Student note: isset($languages[$code]) is useful before accessing a key that may not exist.

questions.text: Using a while loop, generate the even-number sequence starting at 10 and ending at 0, stepping down by two, without writing each number separately.
questions.explanation:
The loop keeps running while n is at least zero, and -= 2 lowers n each round.

Student note: Check the start value, stop condition and update expression to avoid an infinite loop.

questions.text: Create a PDO connection variable named $db for a MySQL database called diploma. Use suitable placeholders for the username and password.
questions.explanation:
PDO is PHP's database access interface, and the DSN identifies the database type, host and name.

Student note: Keep real database passwords outside published source files. Prepared statements are safer for user input.

questions.text: A modules table contains 'Advanced Internet Programming', 'Interactive Programming' and 'Internet Programming'. A query orders rows by module name in ascending order. Which name appears first?
questions.explanation:
Ascending alphabetical sorting places 'Advanced' before both 'Inter...' names.

Student note: SQL ORDER BY name sorts rows by the column value; ASC is the usual default.

questions.text: In an MVC PHP application, which part should normally deal with reading and writing database records?
questions.explanation:
The Model handles application data; the View presents it; the Controller handles requests and coordination.

Student note: Remember MVC as Model=data, View=display, Controller=flow.
